11wbxt: Original SpanishCue material; the situations and data are for teaching, not real news or official exam texts.
apr084: When his daughter announced that she wanted to dedicate herself to restoring musical instruments, Ernesto reacted with a question: «And what are you going to live on?». Clara heard a prohibition, although her father never told her to give it up. For months they argued over a sentence whose meaning both believed to be obvious. He expected her to draw up a plan; she needed him to recognize the seriousness of a choice she had been preparing for years. The conversation did not move forward until they stopped defending words and began explaining concerns.
ec8xs8: Ernesto had grown up in a family for whom having a stable job was a recent achievement. His parents wanted him to study a degree that would let him become independent soon. They did not demand that he become a lawyer, but they celebrated his choice as if he had solved all the family's problems forever. Now he understands that he passed that same pressure on to his daughter, even though he used seemingly more open language. Saying that everyone can do what they want does not eliminate the expectations communicated through silences, jokes, or comparisons.
97yt5a: Clara, for her part, admits that she interpreted any doubt as a put-down. She had researched schools and workshops, but she had not calculated how much it would cost to support herself during the training. It bothered her to be treated as if she were still a child; yet when they asked her for concrete details, she answered that no one trusted her. An aunt stepped in without deciding who was right. She asked each of them to summarize the other's concern before formulating a response.
1e8oc0f: They did not end up thinking the same. Ernesto still considers the profession risky and Clara keeps her project. They agreed to review a budget together and limit family help to a defined period. The change was more modest than a movie-style reconciliation: they learned to disagree without turning every disagreement into a test of affection. For both of them, that was a fairly concrete form of respect.
